speaker: narrator
en: Christian and Pliable went on together across the plain, talking of the country ahead.
source: Part I: 'they drew near to a very miry slough, that was in the midst of the plain' (verify wording)

speaker: pliable
en: Come, let us mend our pace. I long to see those crowns and robes.
source: Part I: 'Come on, let us mend our pace' (verify wording)

speaker: sign
en: Keep moving in the mire, or it will hold you fast.
source: Mechanic hint (mud sinks you when you stand still)

speaker: narrator
en: Being heedless, they both fell suddenly into the bog. Christian, because of the burden on his back, began to sink.
source: Part I: 'being heedless, did both fall suddenly into the bog... because of the burden that was on his back, began to sink in the mire' (verify wording)

speaker: pliable
en: Is this the happiness you have told me of all this while?
source: Part I: 'Is this the happiness you have told me all this while of?' (verify wording)

speaker: pliable
en: If I get out again with my life, you shall have the brave country alone for me.
source: Part I: 'you shall possess the brave country alone for me' (verify wording)

speaker: narrator
en: With that, Pliable struggled out of the mire on the side nearest his own house, and Christian saw him no more.
source: Part I: Pliable gets out 'on that side of the slough which was next to his own house' (verify wording)

speaker: sign
en: By order of the Lawgiver, good and firm steps are set through the very midst of this slough.
source: Part I: 'certain good and substantial steps, placed even through the very midst of this slough' (verify wording)

speaker: sign
en: Do not look at the mire. Look for the steps.

speaker: help
source: Part I: Help asks him what he did there (verify wording)

speaker: christian
en: Sir, I was told to go this way to the gate. Fear followed me so hard that I fled the nearest way, and fell in.
source: Part I: 'fear followed me so hard, that I fled the next way, and fell in' (verify wording)

speaker: help
en: But why did you not look for the steps? Give me your hand.
source: Part I: 'But why did not you look for the steps?' ... 'Give me thy hand' (verify wording)

speaker: help
en: This slough cannot be mended. When a man wakes to his sin, his fears and doubts run down and settle here. That is why it is called Despond.
source: Part I: Help explains the slough 'cannot be mended' (verify wording)

speaker: narrator
en: So Help set him upon sound ground, and bid him go on his way.
source: Part I: 'set him upon sound ground, and bid him go on his way' (verify wording)
